SMTO-EXE-0033 — SMTO couldn't finish working through your data

GUID: 75dabb42-179c-47a4-8922-839d388f022d
Slug: transform-worker-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to sort, count or reshape some data, but that calculation crashed or ran out of time or memory. Earlier results are still saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the failed step and read the last line of its error message. It shows whether the data was too big or slow, or whether the calculation itself had a mistake.
  2. If the data is large, ask SMTO in the conversation to handle it in smaller parts, for example one file or a few hundred rows at a time. Smaller parts stay within the time and memory SMTO allows for this kind of step.
  3. If the message names a missing field or a wrong value, tell SMTO and ask it to correct the calculation and try again. A mistake in the calculation fails the same way every time until it is fixed.

What success looks like

  • The step completes and shows the full result you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete earlier results or remove data you need just to make the step fit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The isolated python.transform worker exited unsuccessfully (including CPU, 256 MiB address-space or time limits) or returned an exception raised by the submitted transform code.

What this means

  • The isolated transform process exited unsuccessfully or returned a serialized transformation exception. The parent category combines worker/resource failure with errors in submitted transformation logic. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The isolated transform process exited unsuccessfully or returned a serialized transformation exception. The parent category combines worker/resource failure with errors in submitted transformation logic.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect bounded worker status and exception detail, input size and the transform logic; do not assume every failure is memory exhaustion.

How to fix it

  • Read the worker stderr or the returned '<ExceptionType>: message' in the step error (agent_runtime.execution.python.execute_transform). Fix the transform logic for exceptions; for limit failures reduce the input size or split the work, keeping within 4 MiB input, 5 s CPU and 256 MiB memory when operation limits are enforced. Do not discard required inputs or receipts to make it fit.
  • Inspect the transform and input size. Simplify or split the local data transformation without discarding required output.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid transformation completes within the configured limits and returns the complete expected data.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
